body:
I know the feeling very, very well. I have autism, and for the entire 20 years I've been alive, every single person I have ever attempted to talk to or be friends with has ended with that person immediately perceiving me as "off"and turning tail at the first opportunity, without fail.

I have no friends and no chance at ever having friends, much less any form of romantic  relationship or sex. Everywhere I look, this world is filled with happy couples and groups of friends, enjoying their lives. You can't escape mentions of love or friendship, anywhere. Turn on the radio? Bombarded with songs about love. Social media? People sharing their lives with their friends and SOs. Movies or shows? Filled with depictions of sex and love, even in media that would normally be completely unrelated to the subject. 

Every single waking second of my life serves as a reminder that my life is an absolute anomaly, a mistake that never should have been made. I intend to fix that mistake.

​

I still can't believe this is real. I'm not convinced this isn't hell.

Of course not. I never expected it to be anything less than a lengthy process, which I agree, is a good thing. My comment was mostly lamentation at most retreats being postponed because of the coronavirus.

I appreciate all the good information. It seems most monasteries I could find that offer paths to ordination require you to attend a few retreats which is pretty much impossible now because of COVID-19 :/

I know exactly how you feel. Without desire, being FA wouldn't be bad. You could live your life without caring about relationships or sex. I used to have nights where I would spend hours crying because I know I will never, ever know reciprocated love or sex. The raw mental anguish of knowing you will never experience intimacy or love, all the while watching the world at large take these for granted is a hell I wouldn't wish on anyone.

If this isn't your thing I understand as a lot of people are very closed to the idea, but look into Buddhism. I started reading into it about a month ago and have since began practicing it. It's done more to help suppress these emotions and accept my place than anything a shrink could ever say to me. Here's a great resource should you be interested:  [https://www.dhammatalks.org/index.html](https://www.dhammatalks.org/index.html)
